newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end choppy day higher.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end choppy day higher.

text.p: Share prices ended broadly up in a choppy trading session on Tuesday, with action focussed only on select stocks amid continued worries about a possbile increase in prices of petroleum products, dealers said.
"Short-covering pushed up prices near the close, but the market remains weak," said Balaji Narayan, an equities dealer at Prime Broking. "People are not buying into the market."

Shares of Century Textiles crashed nearly 13 percent from the day's high of 2,600 to 2,250, but ended 151 rupees, or six percent down, after the firm shocked analysts by posting a 99 percent fall in 1996/97 (April-March) net profits.
The company blamed adverse market conditions in cement and paper and teething troubles at its Bagasse-based plant among the major factors for the steep fall in net profit.
The issue of one bonus equity share for every one share held failed to lift the market gloom over the firm's poor results.
"The market was very topsy-turvy," said Sanjeev Choithani, chief dealer at brokers Pashupati Advani."

"With the budget expected to be passed safely, there was some buying by local institutions and speculators." Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Tuesday said he would examine demands of Left Front parties for changes in the pro-market budget.
"I have heard their views. Let us see how much we can accommodate, how many suggestions are acceptable. We will examine it," Chidambaram told Reuters after a two-hour meeting.
The Left parties have objected to budget proposals on insurance, duties and taxes on personal income and dividends.
The looming worry over the petrol price hike restricted operators from making fresh commitments, traders said.

Shares of Indian Rayon dropped 9.75 rupees, or 2.4 percent, to 393.0 after the firm offered investors one bonus equity share for every two shares held. The bonus announcement was mostly in line with market expectations, traders said.
